This Mfa Is Filed U/S.173 (1) Of Motor Vehicles Act,
Against The Judgment And Award Dated 24.07.2019 Passed
In Mvc No. 311/2015 On The File Of The Senior Civil Judge
And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kushtagi, Awarding
Compensation Of Rs. 6,64,000/- With Interest At 6% P.A
From The Date Of Petition Till Its Realisation.
These Appeals, Coming On For Admission, This Day

Vijaykumar A. Patil, J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

MFA No.102757/2020 is filed by the wife and children of the deceased Siddappa and MFA No.101918/2020 is filed by the mother of the deceased Siddappa being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 24.07.2019 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kushtagi in MVC NO.311/2015 seeking for enhancement of compensation.

2. Brief facts giving raise to filing of these appeals are that wife and two children of deceased Siddappa filed petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking for compensation in respect of death of Siddappa S/o. Sangappa Angadi in a road accident took place on 19.08.2015 at 3.20 p.m.

It is averred that deceased was on the motorbike proceeding from Hanamasagar to Ilkal road and when he reached near Ilkal, the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-26/F-786 came in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the motorbike driven by the deceased Siddappa, he sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to those injuries.
Nirmal W/O. Siddappa Angadi vs Timmanna S/O. Honnappa Wadder on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156764843/
3 3.
It is further averred that the accident has caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver and they are liable to pay compensation.

It is also averred that the deceased Siddappa was a businessman getting income of Rs.30,000/- p.m. and the appellants were depending upon the income of the deceased, they have lost love and affection hence, sought for compensation.
4. The respondents entered appearance before the Tribunal.

The respondent No.2 has averred that the petition is not maintainable as the deceased was not having a valid licence to ride the motorcycle and has violated the provisions of the Motor Vehicle Act and Rules made thereunder and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. The Tribunal framed the issues, recorded the evidence of the parties.
The appellant No.1 who is the wife of the deceased examined herself as PW-1 and daughter of the deceased examined herself as PW-2 and exhibited Exs.P-1 to P-9.
Respondent examined RW-1 and no documents were marked.
The Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.6,64,000/- on different heads with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition till realisation.

6. Learned counsel Sri Shivanand Malashetti for appellants in M.F.A.No.102757/2020 submits that the Tribunal has committed error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- p.m. as they have specifically pleaded that the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

It is submitted that the Tribunal has committed error in not awarding any compensation towards future prospects and granted meager compensation on other heads also and sought for enhancement of compensation.

7. Learned counsel Sri K.H. Bagi for the appellant in M.F.A.No.101918/2020 submits that the appellant is the mother of the deceased Siddappa and the claim petition has been filed by the wife and children of the deceased without arraying her as a party to the proceedings before the Tribunal.
It is submitted that the mother of the deceased was a dependant hence, she is entitled for the compensation awarded as well as the enhanced compensation.
It is further submitted that he supports the case of the appellants/claimants wife insofar as enhancement of compensation.

8. Per contra, Sri Madanmohan M. Khannur learned counsel for respondent KSRTC supports the impugned judgment and award and submits that the Tribunal has considered the evidence on record and assessed the income of the deceased based on the evidence on record.

Awarded compensation is just and proper and does not call for any enhancement in the present appeals and sought for dismissal of the appeals filed by the claimants as well as the mother of the deceased.
9. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for the Corporation.
Perused the material available on record.

The points which arise for consideration in these appeals are:
1) Whether the Tribunal is justified in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- p.m.?
2) Whether the appellants are entitled for the enhanced compensation?
Nirmal

sentences.text: The answer to the above points are in the negative and affirmative respectively for the following reasons:
It is not in dispute that the appeal in M.F.A.No.102757/2020 is filed by the wife and daughters of the deceased Siddappa.
M.F.A.No.101918/2020 is filed by the mother of the deceased Siddappa who was not a party before the MACT.
It is also not in dispute that in the road accident that took place on 19.08.2015 the said Siddappa succumbed to the injuries.

The claimants before the Tribunal have pleaded that the deceased Siddappa was a businessman and was getting income of Rs.30,000/- p.m. and basing on the said pleading, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- p.m.
11.

The Tribunal has awarded the compensation on the following heads:
Towards loss of dependency Rs.6,24,000/- Towards funeral expenses Rs.10,000/-
Towards loss of consortium Rs.5,000/- Towards transportation of dead body Rs.5,000/- Towards loss of love and affection Rs.20,000/-
Total Rs.6,64,000/-
12.

On careful scrutiny of the evidence available on record, it is evident that there is no material placed before the Tribunal with regard to the income of the deceased hence, the Tribunal has proceeded to assess the income of the deceased notionally.
In our considered view, the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased notionally at Rs.6,000/- pm.

Normally this Court and the Lok Adalaths while settling the claims arising out of the motor vehicle accidents rely on the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority while assessing the income in the absence of evidence on record.

The accident is of the year 2015 as per the chart,
the notional income is required to be assessed at Rs.8,000/- pm.

Hence, we assess the notional income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- p.m.
13.

The Tribunal has deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses of the deceased,
which needs no interference.

The deceased was aged 50 years and the multiplier '13'
adopted is proper and correct.
The Tribunal has failed to award compensation on the head of 'future prospects'.

In terms of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
- 10 - Pranay Sethi and others the claimants would be entitled for adding 25% of the assessed income towards 'future prospects'.

The appellants in M.F.A.No.102757/2020 being the wife and children of the deceased are entitled for 80% (2017) 16 SCC 680 - 11 - of the compensation and the appellant in M.F.A. No.101918/2020 being the mother of the deceased is entitled for 20% of the compensation.

16. For the reasons recorded supra, we pass the following :
ORDER i) Both the appeals are allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 24.07.2019 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kushtagi, in MVC NO.311/2015 is modified and the appellants are entitled to the total compensation of Rs.13,60,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation.
iii) The appellants in M.F.A.No.102757/2020 are entitled for 80% of the compensation amount and the appellant in M.F.A.No.101918/2020 is entitled for 20% of the compensation amount.
iv) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement of the share of wife and children of the deceased i.e., 80% of the compensation shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal and the share Nirmal W/O. 6 - 12 - of mother of the deceased i.e., 20% of the compensation shall be released to the mother of the deceased.
v) Registry is directed to transmit the records to Tribunal.
vi) Draw modified award accordingly.
vii) No order as to costs.
